findings.title: CS-2 pg_temp domain control (a) cannot pass and its marker cannot detect execution in a refused statement
findings.claim: The authored control at mjs:1470-1479 creates pg_temp domains named jsonb, uuid and text in the writer session. It then expects content.emptyUpdate and content.update on research_product_content to succeed, and asserts zero marker rows. Reasoning from the documented rules (pg_temp is searched first for data type names, and an object is visible only if nothing with the same name appears earlier in the path), pg_catalog.text, uuid and jsonb are not visible in that session. The guard computes its column descriptor with format_type on every guarded statement (src:1126-1130), before the zero-row return at :1225. With those types hidden, the rendering qualifies them, the digest stops matching the install-time trigger comment, and both statements refuse with 55000 'Quick Order protected source columns drift'. The same holds for the integrity and fingerprint renderings. The source is therefore fail-closed and safe, but the control throws. Its marker is also transactional: an INSERT into a temp table is rolled back when the statement errors. So zero marker rows would be seen even against revision 1, whose unqualified `::text[]` and `::jsonb` casts would have run the marker as owner before refusing. CS-2's required negative is therefore neither reachable nor discriminating.
findings.evidence: mjs:1472-1479; src:1126-1130 (descriptor digest via pg_catalog.format_type, before the changed='[]' return at :1225); research-products-diagnostics.sql:333-335 (uuid and text columns). From the docs: runtime-config-client search_path ('If it is not listed in the path then it is searched first (even before pg_catalog)... only searched for relation ... and data type names'); functions-info visibility functions and datatype-oid ('display schema-qualified names on output if the object would not be found in the current search path'). That format_type itself qualifies non-visible names is not stated in the docs: PLAUSIBLE, NOT RUN.
findings.fix: Make the marker non-transactional, for example nextval on a temp sequence inside pg_temp.doc80_mark(), or capture a RAISE NOTICE on the client. Then expect 55000 'Quick Order protected source columns drift' for both the zero-row and the material statement, with the head and revisions unchanged and zero marker invocations. Add a twin that drops the shadowing domains and shows the same statements succeed (zero-row: no change; material: +1 and held). Disclose that pg_temp type shadows in a session make every guarded statement in that session refuse, including zero-row and OUT ones. This affects only that session and is fail-closed.

Upheld. mjs:1478 runs content.emptyUpdate and content.update with no expected-refusal handling, so any refusal throws. Both statements reach the guard's descriptor check (src:1126-1130) before the zero-row return at :1225. With pg_temp domains named text, uuid and jsonb, those pg_catalog types are not visible (runtime-config-client: pg_temp is searched first for type names). format_type therefore renders them qualified and the digest mismatches. That last step is source-level knowledge (format_type_extended qualifies when TypeIsVisible is false). The functions-info docs describe format_type only as 'the SQL name' and say nothing on qualification, so the mechanism is PLAUSIBLE, NOT RUN. Both halves of the finding rest on that step:
- If format_type does qualify, rev2 refuses, so the control throws.
- Revision 1 refuses too, so the transactional marker insert is rolled back and the marker cannot tell the revisions apart.

Fix refinement. The proposed nextval or insert marker runs as the definer against objects the writer owns. A non-superuser owner then fails on privileges, and plpgsql binds declaration types once per session at first compile. Use a privilege-free signal that is not rolled back: a RAISE NOTICE from the marker, captured by the client. Assert zero notices whatever the statement outcome. Pin the expected outcome (55000 'protected source columns drift' or success) only after S3 establishes format_type behaviour, and keep the twin without the shadowing domains.

Upheld, but narrowed. The claim that control (b) 'would pass against revision 1 as well' is overstated. Revision 1's fingerprint_sql read pg_trigger and pg_class unqualified (cur rev1:72, :75, :78). missed.title: CS-5 peer probe reads a table with forced RLS before the guard checks the owner's RLS bypass

findings.title: Drop/recreate guard drift fixtures (wrong alias, column list, argument) do not isolate the predicate they name
findings.claim:
The wrong-transition-alias, guard-column-list and guard-argument fixtures drop the guard trigger and recreate it. A recreated trigger has a new OID with no RHQOC_SOURCE_COLUMNS_V1 comment. Integrity's guard-inventory OR therefore raises 'Quick Order exact platform guard inventory drift' from the obj_description predicate whatever the alias, tgattr or tgargs predicates say.

If the tgoldtable/tgnewtable predicates were deleted from integrity, the CS-13 alias negative would still pass. Alias drift stays fail-closed through the fingerprint and the guard's own runtime identity check, so this is precision. The receipt classification AUTHORED_DRIFT_GROUPS_NOT_ALL_PREDICATE_ISOLATED is generic and does not disclose that the comment loss hides the result.
findings.evidence: mjs:1826-1838: drop trigger, create trigger, enable always, with no comment restored. SQL:697-703: one OR containing tgoldtable/tgnewtable, tgattr, tgnargs/tgargs and obj_description(t.oid,'pg_trigger') is distinct from 'RHQOC_SOURCE_COLUMNS_V1:'||digest. Receipt:1357-1359. REQUEST:1136 discloses only the column-list event-type overlap.
findings.fix: In each fixture, read obj_description of the original trigger before DROP. After the recreate, run COMMENT ON TRIGGER with the captured value inside the same fixture transaction, so the alias, argument or column list is the only drift. Also add a wrong NEW-alias case and, optionally, a material write through the drifted trigger expecting 'Quick Order guard identity drift' (SQL:1114-1122).

findings.title: Static EXCEPTION-discipline assertion is line-anchored and misses inline handlers
findings.claim: CS-7(e) counts only EXCEPTION WHEN at the start of a line. This SQL routinely puts several statements on one line, for example 'raise ...; end if;'. A successor could wrap gate or head acquisition as 'begin perform pg_catalog.pg_advisory_xact_lock(...); exception when others then null; end;' on one line, and the check would still count 2. The runtime controls would not necessarily notice either.
findings.evidence: mjs:1448-1450 uses /^\s*exception\s+when\b/gim and requires count 2. The current matches are SQL:145 and 344. 'raise exception' is never followed by 'when', so the anchor adds nothing.
findings.fix: Count /\bexception\s+when\b/gi anywhere in candidateText. Require exactly 2, and require each to fall inside section(...,'$publication_shape$') and section(...,'$decision_inputs_shape$') respectively.

findings.title: CS-14 ACL, proconfig and owner drift negatives not extended to the named functions and new tables
findings.claim:
The CS-14 fix asked for ACL and proconfig drift on activate_revision, resolve_scope, read_strict_authority, guard_source_write and the four new tables. Drift is exercised only on read_current_authority (proconfig, owner, EXECUTE grant) and authority_scope_members (SELECT grant).

The grant cases expect 'currentness schema drift' from the fingerprint, so the explicit function and table ACL loops are never discriminated. A regression that left one named object out of both the fingerprint's and the loops' name lists would go undetected.

Role denial and the positive 13-function inventory are complete, so this is precision.
findings.evidence: mjs:1839-1842 has single-object drift entries only. SQL:789-818 holds the explicit ACL loops, which run after the fingerprint gate at SQL:709-712. fingerprint_sql:58-61 covers proacl and relacl. Role denial at mjs:1865-1874 covers all 13 functions and 6 tables.
findings.fix: Loop the drift cases over all 13 DOC80_FUNCTIONS: SET a proconfig and change the owner, expecting 'exact function inventory mismatch'; GRANT EXECUTE to anon, expecting 'currentness schema drift'. Loop a table GRANT over all six DOC80_TABLES. Either add one case that changes the ACL without changing the fingerprint (if any exists), or record in remaining[] that the explicit ACL loops are covered only through the fingerprint.

findings.title: Holder and RR-writer sessions inherit the 1s idle_in_transaction timeout across multi-query control windows
findings.claim:
The synthetic ALTER ROLE ... IN DATABASE settings, including idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=1000ms, apply to every postgres session opened after adminSql: writer, observer, holder and contender. Several controls leave the holder, or the RR/SER writer, idle in a transaction while running a refusal plus two six-table snapshots, or a full publish or activation.

If the timeout fires, the next holder or writer query fails with FATAL 25P03 or the session closes. The control goes red, never false-pass, because the holder's rollback and the writer's statement are awaited. But the results become timing-dependent.

Revision 2 makes the CS-6 window wider by adding a refusal and a head read inside it. In the foreign-holder case, an early kill turns the statement into the gateless case and is caught only when the holder's rollback fails afterwards.
findings.evidence: mjs:546 sets writer idleTimeoutMs 1000. mjs:749-751 and 1108-1109: role settings applied before the observer, holder and contender are opened. Holder windows: mjs:971-980 (CS-6), 1523-1526 (foreign gate holder), 1542-1546 (NOWAIT). RR writer window: mjs:1590-1594. The pg_sleep pattern that avoids this is at mjs:856-858.
findings.fix: Keep holder locks inside an active statement (start() with pg_sleep, as at mjs:858), or open fixture-only holder sessions before the role settings, or with idle_in_transaction_session_timeout disabled. Assert the holder's lock is still granted immediately after each refusal, as mjs:978-980 does.

findings.claim:
doc71RunFutureSuites awaits the doc80 suites but returns only the doc71 result families. doc80RunScopeControls builds a 65-case list with classifications, and that list is dropped. The other doc80 suites return nothing.

A run that completes implies no assertion threw, but its output cannot evidence the DOC80 inventories and counts the receipt enumerates, such as AUTHORED_12_PAIRS_24_INVOCATIONS or the 65 CS10 classifications.

The S3 execution receipt can then bind per-control outcomes to the authored inventory.
